_why: Every value-side exclusion in the WEAK ('pass') arm is safe only because something wider backstops it unconditionally for the full spellings. That backstop is this arm. Narrow it, insert an exclusion into it, or make it unreachable, and a real password can publish with an empty scrub report.
_when_you_may_change_this: When you deliberately widen or narrow what the backstop arm matches. You have to extract the live pattern, JSON-escape it, and update pattern, main_arm and lookaround_counts consistently with what run_tests.sh actually checks, and say in the commit message what is now released and why that is safe. Do not edit this file to make a failing check pass without doing that reasoning first. Note what this file cannot do: SUPERSET compares the shipped arm's text to a COPY OF ITSELF frozen here, so it detects an insertion or a rewrite, never a narrowing that was present the moment this file was last regenerated. If you are regenerating this file BECAUSE you found such a narrowing, that fact belongs in the finding, not just in a wider pattern here.
_main_arm_note: main_arm is the literal tail of the shipped pattern from the '|' that separates it from the WEAK arm through both closing parens, checked with str.endswith. Proves the arm is PRESENT and unaltered character-for-character, never that it is REACHABLE: text inserted before this arm, or a gate placed around the whole union, would not be caught here (see the run_tests.sh comment this baseline is read from).
_lookaround_counts_note: Counts of literal (?= (?! (?<= (?<! substrings anywhere in the shipped PASSWORD_ASSIGN pattern. Every narrowing built against this rule so far added at least one lookaround, so an increase is treated as a narrowing until shown otherwise; a decrease is usually a widening. Unchanged by ROW-150/151/152: still 4/19/0/1.
